whyThisShow: This is the closing night of the April 1971 Fillmore East run, later officially released as 'Ladies and Gentlemen... the Grateful Dead,' which puts it squarely in the canonical Pigpen-era record. One reviewer calls it "the final Fillmore East" and declares it "essential listening material" [source: 'the final Fillmore East is essential listening material.']. Another listener, who has been living with this run since the mid-eighties, holds the Alligator sequence and the Midnight Hour among "the best music I have ever heard" [source: 'the Alligator>Cold Rain has to be some of the best music I have ever heard. Also love the Midnight Hour.']. One reviewer with nearly four decades of listening places 1971 as "the peak of rock music as a 'genre'" and credits this recording with earning six stars [source: 'In my opinion 1971 was the peak of rock music as a "genre", with more great music than any other year.']. One voice does add a partial caveat — loving roughly half the setlist deeply while skipping the rest — so this is not a show everyone takes as a uniform peak from first note to last [source: 'It\'s definitely in my top 10 for about 50% of the songs (the other half I skip over).'].
listenFor: The opening Truckin' is the first place to plant your ears: one listener hears Bobby's shout of "Hey man, go back to 1959!" after it and wonders aloud whether that was a reaction to Garcia's "throwback riffs throughout this Truckin'" [source: 'Was always curious if Bobby\'s comment after Truckin\' ("Hey man, go back to 1959!") was a reaction to someone in the audience shouting a request, or a comment on Garcia\'s throwback riffs throughout this Truckin\'']. The Hard to Handle draws specific attention from at least one listener who calls it "awesome" while noting the commercial release's choice to use this version over the April 22 performance [source: 'This Hard to Handle is awesome, but my favorite Weir solo for this song is from 4-28 , and for the Jerry solo and Phil bombs and the Pig rap I strongly prefer 4-22-71.']. One listener points to Phil's bass on Sugar Magnolia as a standout moment [source: 'Phil\'s bass on Sugar Mag']. The Alligator sequence, described by one reviewer as a moment where the band was "clearly unwilling to play the tail end" and instead carved "new space out enroute to GDTRFB," is singled out as one of the era's high points [source: 'As they find thier way out of alligator, clearly unwilling to play the tail end (recognizing this isnt\' 67, they carve new space out enroute to GDTRFB which is unique and highly valued by this head.'].
context: This is the final night of a five-show Fillmore East stand in late April 1971, recorded from the soundboard and later officially released as 'Ladies and Gentlemen... the Grateful Dead.' The SBD source (identifier gd71-04-29.sbd.frisco.16782.sbeok.shnf) gives it clean separation across the full band. The era is the Pigpen-fronted early-70s lineup, and one reviewer argues this represents "Pigpen and the rest of the Dead at their best" [source: 'I believe this music is Pigpen and the rest of the Dead at their best.']. The run as a whole was bookended each night by Truckin' as the opener, making the final night's version a deliberate send-off for the venue.
funFact: One listener notes that hearing "Bill's talk btw encores about stop asking for more more from the band, sounds a lot like record-bigwigs complaining about downloads" — a 1971 between-set moment that aged into something stranger [source: 'Listening to Bill\'s talk btw encores about stop asking for more more from the band, sounds a lot like record-bigwigs complaining about downloads, strange.'].
headline: Closing night at the Fillmore East, Pigpen still in command.
